title: Skull from above: bones and sutures (superior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Forehead and the roofs of the orbits.
Parietal bones at the coronal suture, and the sphenoid, ethmoid, nasal, lacrimal and zygomatic bones and the maxillae.
Supraorbital margin with its notch or foramen; the frontal sinuses lie within it.
Side and roof of the cranial vault, one on each side.

Frontal bone at the coronal suture, the opposite parietal bone at the sagittal suture, the occipital bone at the lambdoid suture, the temporal bone at the squamous suture, and the greater wing of the sphenoid.
Crosses the roof of the skull from side to side and ends on each side at the pterion. In the midline it meets the sagittal suture at a point called the bregma.
Frontal bone in front from the two parietal bones behind.
hy: In a baby the anterior fontanelle lies at the bregma and usually closes by 18 to 24 months. A tense, bulging fontanelle in a quiet baby suggests raised pressure inside the skull; a sunken one suggests dehydration.

rows: Midline of the roof of the skull, from the bregma in front, where it meets the coronal suture, to the lambda behind, where it meets the lambdoid suture. The superior sagittal sinus runs just beneath it.
Right parietal bone from left parietal bone.
hy: Early closure of a suture (craniosynostosis) affects this suture more often than any other. The skull cannot widen, so it grows long and narrow (scaphocephaly).
